label: sec:mw-rewrites
title: Rewrite Rules
html:
The rewriter RWB​ of [7] consists of width-independent rewrite rules lifted from the rewriter of cvc5 for fixed-size bit-vectors [7, Appendix A]. These rules miss identities that multi-width problems rely on. Table 5 lists the rules without side conditions by which we extend RWB​. The rules with source [35] are axioms of ParaBit, where ∼to-pbv(k,0) is the all-ones bit-vector of width k. Since ParaBit saturates an e-graph, its axioms are bidirectional, and we orient them towards the smaller integer translation (e.g., −Bx translates to a single mod term, whereas ∼x+B1 does not). The new rules handle extensions (zero extension and sign extension), shifts, if-then-else and parametric integer and more powerfully. In [7], a signed comparison at width k is translated via the conversion uts(x)=2⋅(xmod2k−1)−x, which introduces a mod by 2k−1 for each operand. Instead, flip rewrites it into an unsigned comparison of the operands with their sign bit flipped: the bit-vector addition of 2k−1 maps the negative values onto [0,2k−1) and the non-negative ones onto [2k−1,2k), in order. This does not add a new instance of exp, since the reduction of instances of Section 4.4 expresses 2k as 2⋅2k−1.

Extended table: all rewrite rules of the PBV rewriter (cvc5 src/theory/pbv/rewrites)
